findings.title: TOCTOU race condition between device count check and insert
findings.body: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the code first calls `CountDevices` to check if the limit is reached, then proceeds to INSERT if below the limit. Between these two operations, concurrent requests can also pass the count check and insert, causing the actual number of devices to exceed the configured `deviceLimit`. Under high concurrency (e.g., many new anonymous users arriving simultaneously), the limit can be significantly exceeded. Consider using a database-level constraint, an atomic INSERT with a subquery check, or a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE pattern to make the check-and-insert atomic.

findings.title: COUNT query executed on every non-cached anonymous request when device limit is set
findings.body: When `deviceLimit > 0`, every call to `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (i.e., every anonymous request not served by the 29-minute local cache) executes a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ...` query. On a busy instance with many anonymous users, this adds a full table scan (or index scan) to the critical authentication path. Consider caching the count result for a short period or using an approximate count mechanism.

findings.title: TagDevice changed from async to synchronous, adding latency to every anonymous authentication
findings.body: Previously, `TagDevice` was called in a goroutine with its own timeout, so it did not block the authentication response. Now it is called synchronously on the request context. When `deviceLimit > 0`, this adds at least one COUNT query (and potentially an INSERT or UPDATE) to the critical path of every anonymous request. This increases authentication latency for all anonymous users, even those whose devices are already known. The local cache mitigates this for repeat requests within 29 minutes, but first requests and cache-expired requests will pay the full cost.

findings.title: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for devices that exist but have stale updated_at
findings.body: The `updateDevice` function's WHERE clause includes `updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` with a 30-day window. If a device exists in the database but its `updated_at` is older than 30 days (e.g., it was last seen 31 days ago but not yet cleaned up by the background job which runs every 2 hours with a 61-day retention), the UPDATE will affect 0 rows and return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. The device exists but cannot be updated, and the error message doesn't distinguish this case from a truly new device being rejected. This is a minor semantic issue but could cause confusion in debugging.

findings.title: TypeScript type says `number | undefined` but backend always sends a number
findings.body: The `anonymousDeviceLimit` field is typed as `number | undefined` in the TypeScript interface, but the Go DTO uses `int64` without `omitempty`, meaning it will always be serialized as a JSON number (0 when unset). The frontend will never receive `undefined` for this field. If the intent is to distinguish 'no limit configured' from 'limit is 0', the Go struct should use a pointer type with `omitempty`, or the TypeScript type should just be `number`.
